candidates.source_summary: Crawley bag first win of season with victory at Rochdale Largs and Millport News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Crawley Town got their League Two season up and running with a 2-1 win at Rochdale. The Red Devils, who only escaped relegation on the final day of last season, had lost their opener at home to Crewe when they finished with nine men. Crawley went ahead in the eighth minute through Peterborough loanee Pemi Aderoju, who fired home from a left-wing cross by Osman Kamara, his first goal for the club, as they were the more dangerous side in the opening half. Dale started the second period strongly and equalised in the 54th minute when centre back Ethan Ebanks-Landell headed home Ryan East’s header at the far post, only his seventh goal for the club in 154 matches. However, Crawley regained the lead in the 72nd minute through Louie Watson’s penalty after a trip by Kaiden Wilson on Aderoju. The loss left newly promoted Dale, who were heavily beaten at Newport in their first game in the EFL since 2023, still searching for their first point of the campaign.

candidates.source_summary: A three-year-old boy is fighting for his life in hospital after reportedly falling from a first-floor window in Rochdale on Saturday afternoon, Greater Manchester Police said
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A three-year-old boy is fighting for his life in hospital after reportedly falling from a window in Rochdale. Emergency services were called to Spotland Tops, in the Cutgate area of the town, shortly after 4.15pm on Saturday. Police and paramedics responded to the incident at the residential estate, with an air ambulance also spotted landing nearby. Our sister title the Manchester Evening News understands that a three-year-old boy fell from a window on the first floor of a property. Greater Manchester Police said a child was taken to hospital, where he is currently in a critical condition. A force spokesperson said: "We were called today (22 August 2026) at around 4.16pm to reports [of] concern [for] the welfare of a child on Spotland Tops, Rochdale. "Emergency services attended and the child was taken to hospital for treatment, where he remains in a critical condition. Enquiries into the full circumstances around this incident are ongoing."

candidates.source_summary: Matt Taylor hails dream start as Exeter make most of early goal to beat Rochdale Lancashire Telegraph
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Exeter manager Matt Taylor hailed a dream start for his side as a brace of early goals earned them a 2-0 win against Accrington Stanley in League Two. After a Devon Derby defeat to Plymouth in the Carabao Cup and losing 1-0 at Grimsby last week, there was a bit of anxiety around St James Park, but captain Jack Fitzwater settled any nerves inside two minutes with a terrific bicycle kick finish. Ten minutes later, it was 2-0 as a Gwion Edwards shot took a wicked deflection of Accrington skipper Seamus Conneely before ending up in the net. Exeter were rarely troubled as they saw out the rest of the game with ease. “I am delighted and I was so pleased with the start,” Taylor said. “We were front foot, aggressive, put the ball in the box. “People can say it’s an ugly part of the game, or a new part of the game, but the long throw is a weapon and we got first contact and then second ball and the ball is in the back of the net. “There was nothing better than that start and then we added to it and while you are never really comfortable in a game of football, I thought we managed the game really well from that point on. “We would like to – and probably should have – scored another, but we protected our goal really well today. “A lot was made after the first game at Grimsby, but we were one game into a new season and I sensed an anxiety and a stress amongst the fans. We felt that win wasn’t too far away and to get ahead so early in that manner really settled the team down.

It is hoped that such close proximity to elite level athletes could inspire the next generation’s Paul Scholes or Keira Walsh, who both grew up in the local area. The new sports complex would also connect to Bowlee Community Park via a number of footpaths and cycle routes, according to planning papers. If approved, all these homes would be delivered over several years and split into three parts – north, south and east, bisected by Heywood Old Road (the A6045). The southern parcel is expected to deliver around 800 homes, with 550 in the north and 200 in the east. This proposal, separate from the sports complex, would also include a local centre with a primary school, shops and health facilities. This housing scheme, called Simister Bowlee, forms part of a wider plan for the region – called the Northern Gateway. candidates.source_summary: Rochdale play their first home game in the EFL for more than three years on Saturday and the Manchester Evening News has been behind the scenes in the build-up
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The Crown Oil Arena is awash with activity. Rochdale are preparing for their first home fixture in the EFL since May 2023 when Crawley Town visit on Saturday and the ground is undergoing something of a transformation. Fittingly for a club who specialised in late drama on their way to promotion from the National League last season, the finishing touches are still being applied just 24 hours ahead of kick-off. Dale enjoyed a season like no other last term, scoring a host of late goals to take their National League title fight with York City to a final day shootout, which ended in heartbreaking fashion after an added time Dale goal was cancelled out by a 103rd-minute strike from the visitors, handing the Minstermen the title and condemning Jimmy McNulty's side to the play-offs. Rochdale rallied, beat Scunthorpe to make the final, scored a 97th-minute equaliser to come from 2-0 down at Wembley to force extra time against Boreham Wood, and then prevailed in the subsequent penalty shootout. Those three fixtures were CEO Laura Thomas' first three at the club. Talk about a whirlwind introduction. "People kept telling me it's not usually like that," she laughs as she chats to the Manchester Evening News on the eve of the new campaign. That mad fortnight was replaced by a hectic summer on and off the field. Manager McNulty departed for Stockport County , with Ian Watson brought in from South Shields to replace him. Dale are in double figures for both signings and departures and off the pitch the club have undergone a sizeable summer transformation. Everything from bars to the boardroom, catering to cabling, it's been all change. Promotion has hastened some of the work, given the regulations required by the EFL, but the opportunity has been taken to undergo a wider upgrade to some of the tired aspects of their home for nearly 120 years. A safe standing section has been introduced, the pitch - a cause of problems in the past and one that was upgraded in the middle of last season - has been relaid and the National League play-off trophy, won in such dramatic circumstances after a campaign even the best Hollywood screenwriters would struggle to script, is being installed in a glass cabinet halfway up the stairs behind the main entrance. It's a first trophy in the club's history and it will take pride of place as they embark on a new season. candidates.source_summary: A senior delegation from Austria has visited Bury Market to learn more about the success of one of the UK's most celebrated markets and its role in supporting the wider town centre economy.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The visit brought together representatives from Austria's town centre management sector with local market and council leaders. During the visit, delegates toured the market's bustling trading areas, explored the surrounding retail offer, and viewed the nearby Casewell's development.

Representatives from Bury Council and industry bodies, including Market Service Manager Simon Green, Councillor Gavin McGill, and the CEO of NABMA David Catterall, shared insights into the market's award-winning success, the town centre masterplan, and the council's long-standing support for the market as a key driver of economic growth and community life.

The delegation specifically requested a visit to Bury as part of work on the Danube Culinarium Tulln project. Located on the banks of the River Danube, Tulln is developing a new market facility and was keen to learn how Bury has built and maintained a thriving market destination, overcome challenges and planned for future growth.

Roland Murauer, Chief Executive Officer of CIMA (Austria City Centre Management), said:

"England's pioneering role in the field of town centre and high street development, already well known on the continent, was impressively reaffirmed during this professional study tour to Bury.

“In particular, the long-term strategic and operational cooperation between the various stakeholder groups and local government offers valuable insights for us in Austria.

“During this study tour of market halls in England, we gained many interesting insights in Bury for our planned Danube Culinarium Tulln project in Austria. We were particularly impressed by how well Bury Market is integrated into the commercial zones, as well as the clear boost it provides to the town centre's economic prosperity.

The adjoining Caswell's development will add a huge boost to the town centre when it opens later in the year."

Ged Gibbons MSc, who accompanied the delegation, said:

"The warmth of our reception in Bury was recognised by our friends from Austria. It is clear that Bury has true professionals delivering quality markets, with great product knowledge and first-class operational delivery."

Councillor Gavin McGill, Cabinet Member for Culture, Economy and Skills, said: "In Bury we are rightly proud to call our market world-famous.

"That's why I was very pleased to welcome the delegation from Austria, alongside the market team and industry bodies.

"Talking about Bury's progress through investment in the new market canopy and Casewells, as well as other projects in Bury centre and the wider town, tells the world that Bury is the place to be.

"I look forward to welcoming more such delegations and customers to Bury Market in the future."

The visitors also met market traders, who provided a traditional Bury welcome and showcased local produce, helping demonstrate the unique character and appeal that continues to attract shoppers and visitors from across the region and beyond.

Bury Market is widely recognised as one of the country's leading markets and continues to play a central role in supporting local businesses, attracting visitors and contributing to the ongoing regeneration of Bury town centre.

candidates.source_summary: A key road into Bury town centre has re-opened following improvements making it safer for pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers to travel
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Market Street now has improved access for communities in Fishpool and Pimhole, making it easier to reach local shops, services, public transport, and the town centre by walking and cycling, while reducing reliance on short car journeys.

The scheme included work to Market Street:

  • Two new pedestrian-controlled crossings
  • Two upgraded bus stops
  • One new continuous footpath at the entrance to Bury Athletics Club
  • Separated cycle and pedestrian route from traffic with the shared space widened along the full length of Market Street.
  • One new raised table at the junction with Trinity Street
  • Resurfacing of the whole road from junction with Angouleme Way to 50m south of the junction with Wellington Road.

On Wellington Road:

  • The roundabout was replaced with a CYCLOPS junction which separates cyclists and pedestrians from other traffic
  • Resurfacing of Wellington Road from its junction with Grosvenor Street to the entrance of Grundy Hub field.

The improvements complement recent upgrades at the junction of Market Street and Angouleme Way, at Gigg Lane, and the work taking place at the junction of Parkhills Road and Manchester Road.

Councillor Lucy Smith Cabinet Member for Environment, Climate Change, and Operations said: “I’d like to thank everyone for their patience while these key improvement works have been carried out.

“These changes should make it easier and safer for people to walk, cycle or use mobility aids for everyday trips, such as going to school, work, or the shops.

“Thank you for everybody’s patience while these works were done, particularly for people travelling along Manchester Road while we improve the junction with Parkhills Road.

“The work has been timed for the school holidays to minimise disruption, and once the new signals are in place we will carry out the resurfacing work at night.”

The £5.7m Fishpool and Pimhole Active Travel Scheme forms part of the Bee Network and is funded through the UK Government’s City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement (CRSTS) and the Mayor of Greater Manchester’s Challenge Fund.

Work is ongoing at the junction of Parkhills Road and Manchester Road improving the junction and installing new traffic crossing signals.

Once this work is finished Manchester Road will be resurfaced between Gigg Lane and Ashlor Street with night closures and signed diversions. This work is expected to start during the early part of September.

candidates.source_summary: A man has been charged in connection with the terrorist attack at the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim, an Iraqi national of St. James Road, Higher Broughton, has been charged with failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity under Section 38b of the Terrorism Act 2000.

Hakim, whose self-defined ethnicity is Asian, has been remanded to appear before Westminster Magistrates Court today.

The charge relates directly to the antisemetic terrorist attack which took place on the morning of Thursday 2 October 2025, during the holiest day of the Jewish calendar, Yom Kippur, where three were killed, including the attacker, Jihad Al-Shamie, and three more were injured.

Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were sadly killed. All of the three who were injured have since been released from hospital.

Assistant Chief Constable Rob Potts, who holds operational responsibility for Counter Terrorism Policing North West, said: “I can confirm that, earlier today, officers from Counter Terrorism Policing North West charged a man with failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity. This charge is directly related to the terrorist attack which took place at the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue last October.

“This is a significant development in our investigation, and my thoughts are with all those affected by the attack, particularly the bereaved loved ones and survivors. We have updated them and continue to offer them as much support as possible.

“Since the attack took place, we have been unwavering in our commitment to establishing the full picture behind the incident and identifying anybody who may have been involved in any way.

“The charge that has been authorised is the culmination of a substantial amount of meticulous work by the investigation team, supported by the Crown Prosecution Service, and I hope this update reaffirms that commitment.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale will have a chance to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral next week. Jimmy died on August 3, aged 80, after a short illness with his family around him. Known for his clean humour, the Northern Ireland comedian became a household name in the 1970s after working the comedy club scene. Famous for his catchphrase “And there’s more”, he lived in Rochdale and was a big supporter of local charities and causes. On Thursday, August 20, his body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church in Rochdale from 3pm to 5pm on for anyone wanting to pay their respects. His life will then be celebrated at Salford Cathedral starting with a vigil mass for the reception of the body at 7pm. It will be followed by his funeral at 1.30pm on Friday, August 21, at the cathedral, with mourners encouraged to wear bow ties which, along with his Wellington boots, became Jimmy’s trademark. candidates.source_summary: They didn't get away with much
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A deli in Rochdale was broken into but thieves only got away with a can of Fanta and a pack of cigarettes. Rachel Ward only opened the Healey Deli, on Market Street in Whitworth , back in October, but in a short space of time it has managed to build up a reputation for its sandwiches, breakfasts, drinks, and ice cream sundaes. In the early hours of Tuesday morning (August 18), Rachel claimed the shop door was broken into, with thieves smashing a window and using a crowbar to break into a till. But, posting on social media, Rachel said that the incident could have been much worse. Click here for the latest on Manchester's food & drink scene, gigs and more in our CityLife newsletter The cafe owner posted: “WELL… HEALEY DELI HAS OFFICIALLY MADE THE BIG TIME! Unfortunately, we had some unwanted visitors who decided to break into Healey Deli. “After smashing their way in, our criminal masterminds made off with… An emergency packet of cigarettes from the till and ONE Fanta Fruit Twist. That’s it. Not the food, not the coffee, not even the Spam. Apparently the getaway plan required a quick fag and a tropical fizzy drink.” In response to the post, some customers also took the opportunity to make light of the situation. One person posted: "What time do you open in the morning, knowing the spam is safe will pop in for a spam butty." Another said: "Awww Rach, really what was the point, all that damage and they didn't even kidnap the spam!" Despite seeing the funny side of the incident, Rachel told the Manchester Evening News that she was upset over the distress caused by the break-in and the damage that has been caused. She explained: "It is a shame that things like this happen. It is quite hurtful when someone comes in and damages your business that you’ve worked so hard on, especially all for pretty much nothing. We work hard, so it’s very frustrating. “We had to close the business for a day, we’re having to pay to get things repaired. It costs time and money to get these things all fixed and get back on track. It's just something we could have done without. “But I am also aware that there are worse things going on in the world. It’s one of those things where it’s just a case of having to move on from it - the show still goes on. “It has shown me how much of a real community spirit there is in the local neighbourhood. So many people have reached out to me to ask me if they can help me get my door fixed, or get security systems installed. It’s been very humbling.” Lancashire Police confirmed they had received a report of the incident, and are investigating the matter.

A colossal scheme to build 1,550 homes has been earmarked for green fields just off the M60.

The villages of Simister and Bowlee offer a rural lifestyle for local residents, surprisingly located next to one of the north west’s busiest motorway junctions – Simister Island. Sat right on the Bury/Rochdale border, the 98 hectares of farmland will effectively be transformed into a new village.

A new ‘local centre’, a primary school, bus routes, cycle ways and footpaths have all been touted for the project. The site would be delivered over several years and split into three parts – north, south and east, bisected by Heywood Old Road (the A6045). 

The southern parcel is expected to deliver around 800 homes, with 550 in the north and 200 in the east.

The ‘countryside beauty’ would be maintained throughout the site, according to the development framework, with green spaces and ‘pocket parks’ lining the walking and cycling routes throughout. 

The development framework claims this ‘active travel’ network would stretch as far as Heaton Park and link the site to surrounding towns and villages such as Simister next door, Middleton and Prestwich. Transport links to the impending Atom Valley development zone is also on the cards – offering connection to the estimated 20,000 new jobs.

Thousands more homes and the creation of vast amounts of industrial/work space is part of the major overhaul in the north eastern section of Greater Manchester. In Bury, Elton Reservoir is set to gain 3,500 new homes, with a further 1,250 planned for Walshaw. 

Including Simister Bowlee, this would total 6,300 new homes around the area. With this in mind, new transport links are seen as key to connecting the new homes to what is expected to become the largest and most accessible employment and innovation hubs in the region, driving substantial investment into Greater Manchester.

The latest development framework has set out how Simister Bowlee would fit into the wider plan for the region – called the Northern Gateway. 

Like many of the areas targeted in the Northern Gateway scheme, the site is not well served by public transport. It is expected to benefit from the proposed Metrolink extension to Middleton, but that is possibly decades away.

Road infrastructure improvements; bus route enhancements; and the creation of cycle and pedestrian routes would be created initially. The connections across the Atom Valley area would be expected to be established through a new Metrolink tram extension to Middleton and further afield after two decades of development.

The tram-train would be a new public transport vehicle that could travel on both rail lines and tram tracks, without being connected to the overhead lines.

Naturally, there is huge local objection to the major scheme. This is because 1,550 homes are going to be plonked between Simister and Bowlee. 

Residents of Simister Lane, just off Heywood Old Road, are either up in arms or resigned to their fate. None are keen on the scheme being pushed forward by Rochdale and Bury councils but feel they are fighting a losing battle.

candidates.source_summary: Forgotten areas on the edge of Rochdale are set for a makeover thanks to almost £20m in government cash.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Forgotten areas on the edge of Rochdale are set for a makeover thanks to almost £20m in government cash.

The council are set to accept the Pride in Place funding next week at the latest town hall meeting. This means the local authority would get the total £19.6m over the course of the next decade. 

It works out at just under £2m every year for 10 years. The targeted areas are Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield – all of which have been overlooked for funding historically.

Currently no plan has been created to decide on how the cash will be spent. However, tackling congestion; improving parking; creating new green spaces; enhancing local facilities; and expanding maternity services are all early suggestions being made.

At their meeting next week, town hall bosses are also set to approve the Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield Neighbourhood Board – who will establish the proposal on how to spend the money.

The Neighbourhood Board is made up of local community figures; MP Paul Waugh; the council’s regeneration boss Coun Daniel Meredith; and chaired by Laura Rodwell of the M6 Theatre group.

According to council documents, they have until November 30, 2026 to submit their four-year plan to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

This plan is necessary in order to unlock the funding. Some £150,000 has already been granted by the government in order to form the board and generate the plan.

When the Pride in Place funding was announced last year, there was understandable skepticism locally. This was due to the areas going years without proper investment. 

Ken Whittle has lived and worked in the area for decades. He felt very little investment has left the area looking tired and unloved.

Speaking previously, Ken said: “I’m very skeptical about this. People here are used to getting nothing.

“Something for the children will be good or a centre for the community to gather could work because, at the moment, that doesn’t exist.

“Social housing needs work so people can actually come in and have a home. We can’t let it go downhill any further.

“The hardest thing with this is that people are moving out because no one is doing anything with anything. There has been no investment really.

“Maybe this cash can change things, but it’s up to the community to do it properly.”

Another skeptic, Dinah Banks, told the Local Democracy Reporting Service: “I think people just get on with their own lives. Why bother, look at it, it’s got no life at the moment.

“I want to see better GP service and walk-in surgeries and not have to travel so far to get there.

“Maybe a proper community health service. But I won’t hold my breath.”

Rochdale MP Paul Waugh has already held consultation events with locals to get an understanding of what they want. 

Once the new Neighbourhood Board and government cash is formally accepted by Rochdale council’s cabinet on August 25, local views will shape how the future scheme looks.
candidates.source_title: £20m funding for underinvested areas of Rochdale set to be approved - Roch Valley Radio

candidates.source_summary: An old mill in Heywood will be demolished to make way for Heywood’s regeneration.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Regent Mill is an industrial complex rather than the typical historic cotton mill you see dominating the skylines of Rochdalian towns. But the bulldozing of this deteriorating building on St James Street could unlock a wider vision for Heywood.

Rochdale council, who are carrying out the demolition work, say they hope to bring forward plans to build around 200 new homes in this area of the town. 

These homes are expected to be more affordable homes. No timeline for when this could happen has been set out.

Once the former tile merchant has been levelled, it would facilitate housing schemes to come forward, according to the local authority. This would link into Heywood’s ongoing regeneration. 

A fresh new Heywood Civic has already been completed. This has been accompanied by the makeover to Peine Square on the Civic’s doorstep.

Some £20m of the government’s Pride in Place funding is currently being spent, with grant applications for local businesses expected to be open soon. This would bring further cash directly to local organisations to better the area.

Coun Danny Meredith, cabinet member for regeneration and housing at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “The demolition of Regent Mill is part of the wider regeneration of this part of Heywood, as part of our masterplan. This will see us work with partners to transform brownfield sites around the town centre into new, high-quality much needed social homes for local people.

“Over time, we hope to bring forward more than 200 homes on and around the Regent Mill area. So where we now have empty sites, which are not visually appealing, we will have fantastic new homes to help address our housing shortage and give the whole area a lift. 

“We have already seen considerable regeneration within Heywood town centre and this project will continue this redevelopment and further support local families.”

There are some concerns about the demolition work raised by highways teams. Highways explained that recent demolitions of properties in this area ‘have caused damage to highways surfaces causing significant risk to pedestrians’.

Planning papers described how the council intends to fence off the demolition site, including debris netting and site signage to protect pedestrians and the roads.

candidates.source_summary: Residents are hoping a special meeting next week will bring an end to a traffic trial which has caused "bedlam" in Heywood — but highways experts want the six-month trial to continue.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Residents are hoping a special meeting next week will bring an end to a traffic trial which has caused “bedlam” in Heywood — but highways experts want the six-month trial to continue. From July 17, the Hopwood Triangle scheme has seen the closure of Middleton Road at its junction with Manchester Road, close to St John’s Church, to stop drivers using this road as a cut through to access the motorway and link road. Magdala Street has been made one way in the direction of Manchester Road, creating a one-way system at the top of Middleton Road at its junction with Charles Street in the direction of Manchester Road. It has also introduced parking restrictions for HGVs in Coronation Avenue, as well as a 20mph speed limit on residential roads in the area. But since its introduction last month, more than 200 residents have complained about traffic gridlock, near misses and damage to cars — and want the trial stopped. The council has received 242 individual responses to the scheme with 33 (14%) in-support and 209 (86%) objecting. The findings will be discussed at Heywood Township Committee’s extraordinary meting on Thursday, August 27, when many residents hope the plug will be pulled. But officers are recommending that committee continues the scheme for the full six-month trial.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: An MP wants answers from hospital chiefs following reports that patients have died or been harmed because of failures in their care. The Independent and Channel 4 have reported that whistle blowers at Northern Care Alliance claim “patients have died in surgery without adequate investigation, while others had their cancer diagnosis delayed”. The NCA runs Salford Royal Hospital, Fairfield General Hospital, Royal Oldham Hospital, and Rochdale Infirmary. Its 20,000 staff provide care for more than one million people. The Independent and Channel 4 also report that “some patients are alleged to have been left dying or in pain in overcrowded A&E corridors or have been forced to undergo invasive treatments that might have been avoided if their care had not been delayed”. Elsie Blundell, MP for Heywood and Middleton North, said: “Like others locally, I rely on the services of the Northern Care Alliance. I gave birth to my daughter in the Royal Oldham, and my family continues to use that hospital when needed. “I am therefore very concerned to read about the issues within the NCA and, on behalf of local residents, have written to the chief executive to demand an update in person. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man has denied murdering a woman who was found dead in a flat in Rochdale. Kyle Howard, 26, is accused of murdering 44-year-old Keeley Aspinall, who was found in an address on the town’s Freehold estate on May 25. He pleaded not guilty to the single charge. Mr Howard, of Tweedale Street, Rochdale, is now set to go on trial in November. He was remanded in custody by Judge Suzanne Goddard KC. Click here to hear the latest from Manchester's courts in our newsletter A further pre-trial hearing was scheduled for October. The prosecution was represented by Rachel Faux, and the defence by Dan Gaskell during today's (August 19) hearing at Manchester Crown Court. Police were called to reports of a concern for a welfare at the property off Tweedale Street. Ms Aspinall, known to friends as Kiki, was pronounced dead at the scene. In a tribute released through GMP, her family said: "Gone too soon.. we can’t believe you are gone. We will always love you and miss you, love all your family xx." Paying tribute to Ms Aspinall, one friend told the Manchester Evening News she was 'like a sister', adding: "She was the best friend anyone could ask for. I'm going to miss her so much, she will always be in my heart."
